macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street falls ahead of Nvidia earnings
items.summary: U.S. stocks sold off on Monday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 1.41%, the S&P 500 down 1.92%, and the Nasdaq Composite down 2.49%. Semiconductor and other AI-linked shares led losses ahead of Nvidia’s earnings report and Anthropic’s planned IPO.[3]

items.title: Markets raise bets on a December Fed rate hike
items.summary: Hotter-than-expected inflation and hawkish Federal Reserve commentary strengthened expectations for another quarter-point U.S. rate increase in December. Markets were pricing roughly a 94% probability of a hike, while the dollar reached a 19-month high.[5][10]

items.title: Nvidia and Anthropic events put AI rally under pressure
items.summary: Nvidia shares declined as investors awaited quarterly results and assessed uncertainty surrounding CEO Jensen Huang’s reported departure. Anthropic was expected to seek a valuation of about $1.5 trillion in a major Nasdaq IPO later in the week.[3]

items.title: Asian shares retreat amid technology-sector concerns
items.summary: Asian equities weakened ahead of Nvidia’s earnings and Anthropic’s IPO, with Japan’s Nikkei down 0.6% and South Korea’s market down 0.2%. Investors remained concerned that weakening AI-related shares could signal broader doubts about the technology rally.[4]

items.title: Oracle gains after results while Adobe outlook disappoints
items.summary: Oracle rose 2.5% after quarterly results exceeded expectations, while Adobe fell 2.5% after its fourth-quarter revenue forecast midpoint came in below estimates. U.S. inflation also accelerated, with August CPI rising 0.4% after a 0.1% increase in July.[1]

items.title: Oil prices drop as markets reassess inflation pressure
items.summary: Oil prices fell sharply, with crude settling at $85.72 a barrel, its lowest close since August 28. The decline provided some relief to equity investors amid renewed concerns about inflation and interest rates.[6]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum edge lower as crypto market remains under pressure
items.summary: Bitcoin was priced at about $64,883, down 0.7% over 24 hours, while Ethereum stood near $1,820.67, down 0.8%. The broader market continued to face weaker risk appetite and reduced institutional flows.

items.title: 21 banks commit approximately $270 million to Project Faro stablecoin initiative
items.summary: A group of 21 banks, reportedly including Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Santander and Deutsche Bank, committed about $270 million to Project Faro, a planned dollar stablecoin project expected to launch in 2027.

items.title: JPMorgan and DBS launch 24/7 tokenized-dollar transfers between US and Singapore
items.summary: JPMorgan’s Kinexys and DBS introduced an institutional service enabling around-the-clock transfers of tokenized US-dollar deposits between Singapore and the United States. Ant International is the first reported client.

items.title: US regulatory approach reportedly shifts toward narrower crypto oversight
items.summary: A report highlighted the withdrawal of FinCEN’s proposed crypto transfer rule as a potential sign that US oversight may be moving away from broad compliance friction toward more targeted enforcement.

items.title: GLMR jumps more than 10% in one hour
items.summary: Moonbeam’s GLMR token rose 10.21% in a 60-minute period to approximately $0.007586, although the market impact and cause of the move remained unclear.

items.title: Large Bitcoin transfers draw market scrutiny
items.summary: Several major Bitcoin movements involving exchanges and unidentified wallets prompted security and market-monitoring concerns, including transfers totaling hundreds of BTC within a short period.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude for Manufacturing
items.summary: Anthropic introduced a manufacturing-focused Claude plugin with 17 skills and four connectors for tasks including quote drafting, root-cause analysis, production reports and supplier requests.

items.title: NVIDIA announces GR00T 2 and Isaac Lab 3.0
items.summary: NVIDIA launched GR00T 2, an updated open-world action model for robotics, alongside Isaac Lab 3.0, an open-source robot-learning framework.

items.title: Alibaba releases Qwen4-Max
items.summary: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max, a large multimodal model that reportedly outperformed Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.1 and Moonshot’s Kimi K3.1 Pro on coding benchmarks. Independent verification of the reported comparisons was not provided.

items.title: Tencent launches Hunyuan Hy4 flash
items.summary: Tencent reportedly launched Hunyuan Hy4 flash, a lower-cost multimodal model with a 1-million-token context window and availability through Tencent products and its cloud API.

items.title: Moonshot AI expands Kimi into scientific research
items.summary: Moonshot AI partnered with DP Technology to integrate Kimi K3.1 Pro into a biomedical research agent. A demonstration analyzed gene-expression data from 3,696 mouse pancreatic cells and identified 100 candidate genes in about 90 minutes, though the result did not establish autonomous scientific discovery.

items.title: Skild AI open-sources Steel robotics physics solver
items.summary: Skild AI contributed Steel, a GPU rigid-body physics solver, to the open-source Newton engine for robot training. The company reports higher throughput than PhysX across robot-learning benchmarks.

items.title: AI decision models focus on probability outputs
items.summary: Google and OpenAI are reportedly developing decision-oriented AI models designed to return probability estimates rapidly and cheaply rather than produce explanatory responses.

items.title: Perplexity reports more than $1 billion in annual sales
items.summary: Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas reportedly said the AI search company had surpassed $1 billion in annual sales and announced a Frontier Research program intended to coordinate continuously learning AI agents, supported by at least 10,000 GPUs.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launch dominates industry attention
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled to launch on November 19, with analysts expecting one of the biggest entertainment releases ever. Reports cite more than 12 million preorders by November 13 and forecasts of up to 40 million sales by March 2027.

items.title: League of Legends unveils New Dawn update
items.summary: Riot Games released a teaser for League of Legends: New Dawn, a planned 2027 overhaul featuring a modernized client, visual updates to Summoner’s Rift, redesigned characters and bosses, and new ways to play.

items.title: Shinji Mikami targets mid-2027 for Unbound debut
items.summary: Resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami said Unbound, his new studio acquired by Shift Up, expects to release its first game around mid-2027. The project is planned to pursue a novel development approach, though details remain undisclosed.

items.title: Coffee Stain acquires Chronicles: Medieval rights
items.summary: Coffee Stain agreed to acquire Chronicles: Medieval and related assets from bankrupt Danish developer Raw Power Games for DKK 36.75 million. Coffee Stain will own 75% of a new company and fund continued development, with release currently planned for 2027.

items.title: Ubisoft Massive outlines broader studio ambitions
items.summary: Ubisoft Massive chief Christoph Hartmann said he wants the studio to become the “A24 of video gaming,” expanding beyond its established shooter franchises. The studio is working on March of Giants and another unannounced project.

items.title: Cinder City global alpha test announced
items.summary: NC plans a global alpha test for Cinder City from December 4–6 for players in North America, Europe, and Asia. The open-world tactical shooter’s test will include squad dungeons, an expanded mission, and a larger playable world.

items.title: GameSquare reports stronger third-quarter results
items.summary: GameSquare reported 77% year-over-year revenue growth and third-quarter net income of $10.1 million. The company also highlighted creator-intelligence initiatives and said FaZe Esports won another major international championship.
